kings1.1.p1.b1.text: Now King David was old and well along in years, and though they covered him with blankets, he could not keep warm.

kings1.1.p1.b2.text: Let us search for a young virgin for our lord the king, to attend to him and care for him … to keep him warm.

kings1.1.p1.b3.text: Then they searched throughout Israel for a beautiful girl, and they found Abishag the Shunammite and brought her to the king.

kings1.1.p1.b4.text: The girl was unsurpassed in beauty; she cared for the king and served him, but he had no relations with her.

kings1.1.p2.b2.text: And he acquired chariots and horsemen and fifty men to run ahead of him.

kings1.1.p2.b3.text: (His father had never once reprimanded him by saying, “Why do you act this way?” Adonijah was also very handsome, born next after Absalom.)

kings1.1.p2.b4.text: So Adonijah conferred with Joab son of Zeruiah and with Abiathar the priest, who supported him.

kings1.1.p3.b1.text: And Adonijah sacrificed sheep, oxen, and fattened calves near the stone of Zoheleth, which is next to En-rogel. He invited all his royal brothers and all the men of Judah who were servants of the king.

kings1.1.p3.b2.text: But he did not invite Nathan the prophet, Benaiah, the mighty men, or his brother Solomon.

kings1.1.p4.b1.text: Have you not heard that Adonijah son of Haggith has become king, and our lord David does not know it?

kings1.1.p4.b2.text: Now please, come and let me advise you. Save your own life and the life of your son Solomon.

kings1.1.p4.b3.text: Then, while you are still there speaking with the king, I will come in after you and confirm your words.

kings1.1.p5.b1.text: So Bathsheba went to see the king in his bedroom. Since the king was very old, Abishag the Shunammite was serving him.

kings1.1.p5.b3.text: My lord, … you yourself swore to your maidservant by the LORD your God: ‘Surely your son Solomon will reign after me, and he will sit on my throne.’

kings1.1.p5.b4.text: And as for you, my lord the king, the eyes of all Israel are upon you to tell them who will sit on the throne of my lord the king after him.

kings1.1.p6.b2.text: And Nathan went in and bowed facedown before the king.

kings1.1.p6.b3.text: And behold, they are eating and drinking before him, saying, ‘Long live King Adonijah!’

kings1.1.p6.b4.text: Has my lord the king let this happen without informing your servant who should sit on the throne after my lord the king?

kings1.1.p7.b2.text: As surely as the LORD lives, who has redeemed my life from all distress,

kings1.1.p7.b3.text: Surely your son Solomon will reign after me, and he will sit on my throne in my place.

kings1.1.p7.b4.text: May my lord King David live forever!

kings1.1.p8.b1.text: Call in for me Zadok the priest, Nathan the prophet, and Benaiah son of Jehoiada.

kings1.1.p8.b2.text: Take my servants with you, … Set my son Solomon on my own mule and take him down to Gihon. There Zadok the priest and Nathan the prophet are to anoint him king over Israel.

kings1.1.p8.b3.text: You are to blow the ram’s horn and declare, ‘Long live King Solomon!’

kings1.1.p8.b4.text: Amen, … May the LORD, the God of my lord the king, so declare it.

kings1.1.p9.b1.text: Then Zadok the priest, Nathan the prophet, and Benaiah son of Jehoiada, along with the Cherethites and Pelethites, went down and set Solomon on King David’s mule, and they escorted him to Gihon.

kings1.1.p9.b2.text: Zadok the priest took the horn of oil from the tabernacle and anointed Solomon.

kings1.1.p9.b4.text: All the people followed him, playing flutes and rejoicing with such a great joy that the earth was split by the sound.

kings1.1.p10.b1.text: Why is the city in such a loud uproar?

kings1.1.p10.b2.text: Come in, … for you are a man of valor. You must be bringing good news.

kings1.1.p10.b3.text: Our lord King David has made Solomon king.

kings1.1.p10.b4.text: Moreover, Solomon has taken his seat on the royal throne. … And the king has bowed in worship on his bed,

kings1.1.p11.b1.text: At this, all the guests of Adonijah arose in terror and scattered.

kings1.1.p11.b2.text: Let King Solomon first swear to me not to put his servant to the sword.

kings1.1.p11.b3.text: If he is a man of character, not a single hair of his will fall to the ground. But if evil is found in him, he will die.
